title: Individual Construction Practising Certificates 2026: Conditions
desc: Construction practising certificates 2026 (Decree 212/2026): who needs one, grade I-III conditions, dossier, 10-year validity, fines for borrowing certificates.
summary: Which roles need a construction practising certificate, the conditions for each grade, the dossier and the issuing time under the Construction Law 2025 and Decree 212/2026/ND-CP.
body: p

From 1 July 2026, individual practising certificates for construction activities (CCHN) are governed by Article 88 of the Construction Law 2025 and Decree 212/2026/ND-CP. For homeowners, knowing these rules helps check whether the designer or supervisor they hire is qualified.
h2
1. Which roles require a practising certificate?
p

Under Clause 1, Article 88 of the Construction Law 2025, a corresponding CCHN is required when acting as: head or lead of urban and rural planning; head of construction survey; head or lead of construction design or design appraisal; construction supervision; lead in determining, appraising and managing construction investment costs. CCHNs are divided into grades I, II and III. Individuals practising independently in these fields must also hold a CCHN (Article 90).
p

Site commanders, project management directors and inspection leads are not issued certificates but must meet capacity and experience conditions (Clause 2, Article 88; Article 38 of Decree 212/2026/ND-CP). Architectural design follows the law on architecture (Article 28).
h2
2. Cases where no certificate is needed
p

Under Clause 3, Article 27 of Decree 212/2026/ND-CP, a CCHN is not required for: preliminary design and appraisal of preliminary design in a pre-feasibility study report; design and supervision of communications and telecommunications systems within a work; design and supervision of finishing work (plastering, tiling, painting, door installation, etc.) and tasks that do not affect load-bearing structure; and certain works such as greenery, public lighting and telecommunications cables.
h2
3. Conditions for issuance
p
Under Article 33, an individual must have full civil legal capacity, suitable professional training and experience within the most recent 10 years:
ul
Grade I: a relevant university degree and at least 7 years of experience.
Grade II: a relevant university degree and at least 4 years of experience.
Grade III: at least 2 years (university) or 3 years (college).
p

Each field also has its own experience conditions. For example, for grade III construction supervision: having taken part in supervision, design or construction of the corresponding part of 1 work of grade III or above, or 2 works of grade IV (Article 37).
h2
4. Dossier, place of submission, time limit
p
A first-time dossier consists of (Clause 1, Article 39):
ol
An application in Form No. 01 of Appendix III (for online submission, completed on the electronic form).
A 4x6 cm colour photo on a white background, taken within the last 6 months.
The relevant degree (with transcript if the degree does not state the major).
A previously issued CCHN (if any).
A decision assigning work or a confirmation by the project owner of work done; for independent practice, attach the contract and acceptance record.
ul
Submit 1 set directly at the One-Stop Department, by post or on the National Public Service Portal (Clause 1, Article 30).
The provincial People's Committee organises issuance; it may delegate or authorise (Article 31).
Time limit: 6 working days (new issue) from the notice that the dossier is eligible after assessment by the Council; 5 working days (reissue) (Clause 2, Article 30).
A newly issued CCHN is valid for 10 years (Clause 5, Article 27).
h2
5. When is a certificate revoked or a fine imposed?
p

A CCHN is revoked when the holder no longer meets the conditions, forges the dossier, leases or lends the certificate, erases or alters it, etc. (Clause 2, Article 29). An individual engaging in construction activities without being qualified, or borrowing, lending, hiring or hiring out a CCHN, is fined VND 10–20 million; borrowing or hiring also results in suspension of the right to use the CCHN for 6–12 months (Article 13 of Decree 339/2026/ND-CP).
p
A CCHN issued under the Construction Law 2014 may continue to be used until it expires (Clause 5, Article 55). See also Designing Your Own House: When You Must Hire a Design Firm.
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. From 20 May 2026 to the end of 28 February 2027, Resolution 66.18/2026/NQ-CP on cutting business conditions affects Clauses 1 and 2, Article 88 of the Construction Law; our library does not yet have the full text of this resolution. From 1 March 2027, Law 24/2026/QH16 amends Clauses 1 and 2, Article 88, removing the roles leading cost determination, appraisal and management from the list requiring a CCHN. Ask the Department of Construction before submitting a dossier.
